origin: Authored by hand for SP-15. NOT captured from a session, NOT derived from any benchmark corpus, and not a renamed copy of an older fixture. Nothing here carries a provenance label from elsewhere that this file would be overwriting.
signal_under_test: MinHash Jaccard near-duplicate detection (00-ARCHITECTURE.md 8.1 item 1, internal/sketch/minhash.go)

files.tlsclient_permissive.txt: an outbound HTTP client that skips TLS verification
files.tlsclient_hardened.txt: byte-identical except that the same constant is false

difference: one token on line 13: AllowUnverifiedTLS = true vs false
what_it_demonstrates: The pair sits far above the shipped nearDupThreshold of 0.9 and the two documents are not equivalent: one disables certificate verification for every outbound call and the other does not. Similarity is a statement about shingle overlap, not about meaning, and the token that differs is the only one that matters.
qualified_claim_this_supports: analyzer.DetectRedundancy reports NearDups as candidates pending exact verification. Similarity establishes neither equivalence nor an exact delta.
over_claim_this_prevents: Treating a NearDups entry as proof that two results are the same, and therefore dropping, rewriting or delta-encoding one against the other. On this pair that would silently substitute the permissive client for the hardened one, or the reverse.
how_to_verify_exactly: Compare the two content roots. They differ. Root equality is exact and cheap; the sketch is neither.
